title: Zendaya Is Wearing Spider-Man's Colours Now — and the 'Brand New Day' Press Tour Has Become the Best Show in Town
excerpt: Versace chainmail in Rome, leather in Berlin, a 5-carat ring she's no longer hiding, and Tom Holland kissing her forehead between photocalls. The fashion is the marketing now.
body:
The movie doesn't open until July 31. The press tour is already a blockbuster.

Zendaya has spent the back half of June turning the *Spider-Man: Brand New Day* promotional circuit into a moving couture exhibition, and on June 23 in Rome she delivered the look that tied it all together. Stepping out in vintage Versace chainmail from the house's Fall 1997 archive, she wore a royal-blue sleeveless crop top with a matching mini skirt — Spider-Man's own red-and-blue palette, reworked as something far more dangerous than spandex. White stilettos, diamond studs, a Rolex on the wrist, and the whole thing assembled by her longtime co-conspirator, stylist Law Roach, who posted the original runway look to his Stories as if to say: yes, we did our homework.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=62bIsvRcPv0

> Channelling a superhero's suit without ever putting one on — that's the kind of fashion sleight-of-hand only Zendaya and Roach pull off this cleanly.

> "Every forehead kiss, every archival Versace pull, every "hi from Rome" is content — and they are very, very good at it."

https://x.com/geordanavar/status/2069405785814139296

It was a deliberate break from the streak. The day before, in Berlin, she'd gone full noir in a custom Louis Vuitton set — a cropped leather bra top and a low-rise leather skirt with a dramatic train, finished with royal-blue spider-web earrings because the woman commits to a theme. Back on June 15 in Madrid, she'd worn a semi-sheer red number by Spanish label Ernesto Naranjo, all high neckline and thigh-high slit. Black, then red, then blue. If you squint, the entire tour wardrobe is the Spider-Man flag, unspooled across three cities.

And then there's the other story the cameras keep finding: the ring. Days after Tom Holland finally, officially confirmed the two are married, Zendaya walked the Berlin carpet flashing her glitzy stack — the five-carat engagement diamond and a gold band she'd previously worn at the Oscars in March. No more coy single-band appearances. In Rome, Holland leaned in to kiss her forehead during the photocall, and she posted it herself with a breezy "just jumping on to say hi from our stop in Rome." The internet, predictably, did not survive.

Why the diaspora is watching

For Indian and diaspora audiences, Spider-Man has never been a niche concern — the Marvel machine lands in India in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu, and Holland's webslinger in particular has been a multiplex juggernaut from Mumbai to Mississauga. *Brand New Day*, the start of a fresh chapter for the character, is shaping up to be one of the summer's biggest global releases, and a press tour this magnetic is doing the quiet work of turning curiosity into opening-weekend tickets.

It also lands in a season when the line between a film's marketing and its leads' personal mythology has all but dissolved. Zendaya and Holland aren't just selling a movie; they're letting fans watch a real marriage glow at the edges of a fictional one. Every forehead kiss, every archival Versace pull, every "hi from Rome" is content — and they are very, very good at it.

The genius of this run is that none of it feels like a campaign. It feels like two people who are genuinely besotted, dressed by people at the absolute top of their craft, moving through European capitals with the ease of stars who have nothing left to prove. The suit comes out July 31. Until then, the best costume on the *Spider-Man* tour is whatever Zendaya wears to lunch.

The movie will make its money. But the tour? The tour is already iconic.
